notes: Governing documents: the Manual of Staff Policies for Academics and Librarians (2.02.11 Maternity/Parental Leave, 2.02.12 Adoption, 2.02.13 Family Care, 2.02.14 Leave without pay, 2.02.05 Sick Pay), which refers to PDAD&C Memo #33 (2003-04), the Provost's procedures memorandum; and the Policy and Procedures on Academic Appointments (June 26, 2015) for the tenure clock. The HR benefits page and HR news item are summaries. The UTFA Memorandum of Agreement is a framework agreement with no leave terms (Article 6 makes the maternity, parental, family care and sick leave policies negotiable); the 2017-18 Article 6 settlement only renames the compassionate/emergency leave.

Conflicts noted: (1) parental leave length for the birth mother: Manual 35 weeks vs the memo's 52-week total (20 + 10 + 22, i.e. 32 weeks after maternity leave) — both coded, the 52-week cap in leave_limits; (2) adoption leave: memo 17 paid weeks within 37 (adoption only) vs HR page 20 paid weeks within 52, also open to a non-biological-mother primary caregiver after a birth (c10, summary_only); (3) parental waiting-period pay appears only on the HR page (c8, summary_only); (4) leave without pay: Manual (up to normally 3 years, not unreasonably denied) vs HR page (one year, Provost approval) — Manual governs.

Version: the Manual is a 2006 compilation still linked in January 2018; the 2017 settlement amends it, confirming it in force. Its copy of the PPAA (s. 10, 'to accommodate a maternity') is superseded by the June 2015 PPAA. The Manual's maternity provision is written for the two-week EI waiting period; EI's waiting period was one week from 2017-01-01 and the HR news (2017-12-01) says the University was 'working to implement this change'; the employer's terms are coded as written (R21).

Not components: Short-Term Compassionate, Bereavement and Emergency Leaves (Manual 2.02.15, 2017 settlement) — compassionate/bereavement/emergency purposes, like the Ottawa special leaves (checklist §1); research and study leaves, administrative leaves and political candidacy leaves (purpose-specific, not usable for a birth); semi-retirement (age 60-65); Statement on Accommodation for Persons with Disabilities (disability only).
Same-sex partners ineligible for EI parental benefits receive an equivalent University top-up (PDAD&C #33): a path for members not eligible for EI, recorded in c7's note (U8).

Chain, birth parent: maternity leave 20 [ESA pregnancy leave 17 alongside from week 0; waiting-period pay 2 weeks at 95% within, weeks 0-2; EI top-up up to 18 within from week 1; EI maternity 15 from week 1] → parental leave 35 (consecutive after maternity; 52-week cap on maternity + parental; 10-week top-up within from its start) ; ESA parental leave 61 consecutive after ESA pregnancy leave; EI parental 35 consecutive after EI maternity.
Chain, non-birth parent: parental leave 37 [ESA parental leave 63 alongside; EI parental 35 from week 1; 10-week top-up within from week 1; HR-only two-week waiting-period pay within, summary_only].
